title: Keyboard Manager: Mapping Windows Key to Left CTRL causes an issue when entering passwords

status.label: Clarify the remap direction and retest safely
status.detail: The title says Windows-to-Ctrl, but the reproduction steps say Ctrl-to-Windows; those configurations imply different expected behavior.

judgment.rationale: The issue title says Windows Key is mapped to Left Ctrl, but the reproduction says Left Ctrl is mapped to Windows. Pressing a key that is configured to emit Windows could explain the Start menu; if the mapping direction is the reverse, the report may involve remap behavior in a browser password field. The reporter lists PowerToys 0.96.0 and Windows 11 Enterprise but does not state which physical key was pressed. Ask for the exact source-to-target mapping and a safe current-build retest without requesting any password.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys 0.96.0, Microsoft Store installation, and a Lenovo ThinkPad running Windows 11 Enterprise.
The issue title says Windows Key to Left Ctrl, while the steps say Left Ctrl to Windows.
The reported symptom is that the Start menu opens while entering a browser password field; no expected/actual detail or comments resolve the mapping direction.
The issue has no comments or assignees.
Closed issue #13699 documents that Keyboard Manager does not remap keys on the Windows login screen; that does not establish behavior in a browser password field.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask which source-to-target mapping is configured, which physical key opens Start, and whether the same behavior occurs on v0.102.3001 in a non-sensitive test field.

fix_assessment.rationale: The title/body mismatch prevents determining whether this is expected behavior for a Ctrl-to-Windows mapping or a failure to apply Windows-to-Ctrl in a browser field; clarify before selecting a product fix.

proposed_fixes.title: Investigate the reported Windows-key remap in browser input fields
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The reported Start-menu behavior could be expected if Left Ctrl is mapped to Windows, or could indicate a remap exception if Windows is mapped to Left Ctrl; the conflicting mapping descriptions do not identify the failing path.
plan: Confirm the exact source key, target key, and physical key press from the reporter.
Retest on a current supported build in a non-sensitive browser test field and a normal text field; do not capture or share password contents.
If the mapping direction and behavior establish a PowerToys defect, trace the confirmed field/input path and add focused regression coverage.
verification: Confirm the specified physical key produces the expected remapped key without opening Start unexpectedly.
Verify the test uses no real password or secret content.

confidence.rationale: The title and reproduction steps conflict about mapping direction, and the report lacks a clear expected result and current-build test.
